title: Gravity: The Invisible Pull
description: The Baron switches off gravity in one hall and objects drift everywhere! Restore it by mastering the most famous non-contact force.

content.value: Some forces act WITHOUT the objects touching. These are NON-CONTACT forces. The three main ones are gravitational force, magnetic force, and electrostatic force. Gravity is the one you feel every second.

Every object in the universe pulls every other object toward itself. This pull is GRAVITATIONAL FORCE. The Earth is huge, so its gravity pulls everything toward its centre — that is why a dropped ball falls down, why rain falls, and why we stay on the ground.

The gravitational force the Earth exerts on an object is called its WEIGHT. Mass (how much matter is in you) stays the same everywhere, but weight can change. The Moon's gravity is about 1/6th of Earth's, so you would WEIGH six times less on the Moon — even though your mass is unchanged.

MASS  → amount of matter (same everywhere)
WEIGHT → pull of gravity on that mass (changes with gravity)

On the Moon: same mass, but only 1/6 the weight!
Gravity acts over huge distances with nothing in between — that's how the Sun holds the planets in orbit and the Earth holds the Moon, across millions of kilometres of empty space.

Key Takeaway: Gravity is a non-contact force by which every object pulls every other. Earth's gravity pulls things down; the weight of an object is the gravitational force on it, which changes with gravity while mass stays the same.

quiz.question: A non-contact force is one that…
options: can act without the objects touching
quiz.explain: Non-contact forces like gravity, magnetic and electrostatic force act even without contact.

quiz.question: The weight of an object is…
options: the amount of matter in it
the gravitational force acting on it
quiz.explain: Weight is the gravitational pull on an object. Mass (amount of matter) is different and stays the same.

quiz.question: On the Moon, compared to Earth, your…
options: mass and weight both drop to 1/6
mass stays the same but weight becomes about 1/6
mass becomes 1/6 but weight stays the same
quiz.explain: Mass is unchanged, but the Moon's weaker gravity makes your weight about one-sixth of Earth's.
